# Criticality catalog

<!-- Generated by scripts/render_catalog.py from src/detector/criticality.py. Do not edit by hand: run `make catalog-doc`. -->

ClickOps Sentinel rates every console change, and every API change by a
labelled AI agent, against this catalog before the AI investigation runs.
The rating is deterministic, works without Bedrock, and acts as a floor
under the agent's security severity: the
agent can raise it from context, never lower it, and expresses whether
a risky change looks sanctioned through its verdict instead.

## Scale

| Level | Meaning | Expected response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| critical | Disables audit logging or threat detection, changes the AWS Organization or its guardrails, grants administrator access or a cross-account backdoor, or exposes data publicly. | Act now: confirm with the actor and contain. |
| high | Creates credentials or privileges, weakens authentication, opens internet exposure, runs code or commands on existing resources, or destroys data without a recovery path. | Review the same day. |
| medium | Changes a security control with limited blast radius: private-range firewall rules, encryption or key state, backups and retention, account-scoped resource policies. | Review within the week. |
| low | Ordinary resource change with no exposure or privilege change. | Codify in IaC or revert during routine drift cleanup. |
| none | Cosmetic change only, such as tags or descriptions. | No action. |

## How a rating is computed

1. The CloudTrail `eventSource` and `eventName` form a `service:Action` key
   (version suffixes such as `20150331v2` are stripped), matched against
   the rules below.
2. The rule's parameter check, when it has one, inspects
   `requestParameters` and can only raise the level.
3. Modifiers raise the level further: actions by the root user
   (ROOT-001) and actions that target ClickOps
   Sentinel's own resources (SELF-001) are at least
   high, and apply even when no rule matches.
4. A failed call (any `errorCode`) is lowered one level, never below low,
   and marked as an attempt.
5. A session that switches browser (client) or source country between two
   changes is raised to at least high
   (SES-001): it suggests a stolen session cookie or
   temporary credentials replayed elsewhere. This compares the change with
   earlier ones, so it is applied by the detector rather than per record.
6. Critical changes, and changes with a session anomaly, bypass the
   session cooldown, so they are always investigated on their own.

Operators can re-rate actions with the `CriticalityOverrides` stack
parameter, for example `ec2:CreateVpc=high,iam:CreateRole=low`. An
override replaces the catalog level of that action; parameter checks
still apply, so an override cannot hide a public exposure.

References: [MITRE ATT&CK](https://attack.mitre.org/matrices/enterprise/cloud/iaas/)
techniques and [Stratus Red Team](https://stratus-red-team.cloud/attack-techniques/AWS/) attack
techniques, the open-source catalog of known AWS attack techniques.
